title: RBAC v2 attack-surface review and pen-test remediation plan for SSO / audit / admin controls
creator: Miguel Ortiz
description:
Goal: produce a prioritized, actionable remediation plan that addresses findings from the internal threat model and third-party penetration test covering RBAC v2, audit logging, SSO/SAML integration, and admin controls. This ticket coordinates engineering work, security reviews, and rollout gating for the platform-2025.02 release.

Scope and background:
- RBAC v2: new policy engine (policy-language v1 -> v2) and role inheritance introduced in Q4 deployments. Early integration tests passed but pen-test surfaced a combination of configuration and logic-edge issues (privilege escalation via group binding, wildcard resource patterns, and stale role binding cleanup gaps).
- Audit logging: logs are emitted to an internal ELK stack with 90-day retention for prod by default. Pen-test identified gaps in immutable logging paths, insufficient contextual linkage between audit entries and SSO assertions, and missing alerts for admin-token usage patterns.
- SSO/SAML and admin controls: Single sign-on sessions may remain active after server-side role revocation; there is no standardized emergency "break-glass" flow documented. Pen-test demonstrated a medium-severity scenario where SAML assertion replay could be amplified by stale cached RBAC decisions.

Deliverables (high-level):
1) Threat-model delta doc: capture new attack vectors introduced by RBAC v2 (inheritance + wildcard resources), express risk and exploitability, and map to mitigation categories (fix code, runtime checks, detection). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/rbacv2-threatdelta (working draft).
2) Pen-test findings triage matrix: map each finding to owner, remediation approach, estimate, and verification step. Attach: drive/pen-test-2025/rbcaudit-report.pdf (redacted).
3) Remediation PRs and acceptance tests: concrete code/infra changes, with automated regression tests and canary plan. Key PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8412 (RBAC fixes), /pull/8427 (audit pipeline immutability).
4) Observability updates: new audit log schema fields (sso_assertion_id, action_abuse_score, pre_change_role_snapshot), dashboards, and alert rules.
5) Admin controls runbook and emergency flow: documented break-glass, time-limited emergency tokens, and post-event forensics checklist.

Prioritized remediation list (initial):
- P0: Prevent privilege escalation via wildcard role bindings. Implement strict validation in the role parser, add server-side rejection for ambiguous wildcards, and add unit tests. (Owner: ENG-Auth; estimate 3).
- P0: Add SSO assertion linkage to every audit event and enforce assertion freshness checks. Update SAML handler to persist assertion_id, not just subject. (Owner: ENG-SSO; estimate 2).
- P1: Harden RBAC decision cache invalidation on role binding changes: immediate eviction and a short TTL for critical roles. (Owner: ENG-Cache; estimate 2).
- P1: Immutable append-only log path for production audit stream with signed segments (short-term: add HMAC per-batch, long-term: integrate with KMS-signed blobs). (Owner: ENG-Obs; estimate 5).
- P2: Break-glass design and temporary token lifecycle with audit hooks and automated revocation. (Owner: ENG-Admin; estimate 3).

Acceptance criteria (for each remediation):
- Unit + integration tests cover both happy path and malicious replay/edge cases.
- Regression harness includes the pen-test reproduction steps and fails before fix, passes after fix. Link to harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security-tests/tree/main/rbacv2.
- Audit logs include sso_assertion_id and correlation_id fields for every decision event in prod canary cluster.
- Security sign-off: at least two reviewers from Security Guild (one threat model author + one pen-test reviewer) must approve the PR.

Rollout strategy and risk mitigation:
- Staged rollout: dev -> staging (full e2e test with replay checks) -> prod canary (5% traffic) -> full rollout. Canary must run for minimum 48 hours and show no user-facing authorization regressions or excessive latency (>5% p95 increase).
- Fallback: versioned RBAC policy engine feature flag (rbac_v2_safe_mode). If critical regressions appear, flip feature flag to force older evaluation path while fixes are backported.
- Post-deploy verification: automated audit integrity job runs hourly to check HMAC consistency and assertion linkage. Any failure triggers PagerDuty SEV3.

Open decisions and technical trade-offs:
1) Whether to adopt signed append-only segments (higher integrity) vs. HMAC per-batch (faster to implement). Security prefers signed segments; timeline favors HMAC first. We will implement HMAC as a short-term mitigation and schedule signed segments for platform-2025.04.
2) Cache invalidation: immediate global eviction is safest but may cause brief latency spikes under load. Alternative is targeted eviction + short TTL; team prefers targeted eviction plus short TTL to reduce impact.
3) Break-glass UX: should emergency tokens be available only through a separate admin console with SSO-adaptive MFA? Design recommends console + step-up MFA; product trade-off is time-to-respond for on-call.

Verification & tests to run during review:
- Pen-test replay scripts executed against staging using seeded DB of role bindings. Expected: stale decision exploit must fail after fixes.
- Fuzz RBAC policy parser with malformed wildcard rules. Expected: parser must reject ambiguous patterns and log the error.
- Audit replay integrity test: rebuild HMAC chain for a 24h window and verify no tampering.
- SAML assertion replay test: send same assertion twice with different timestamps to ensure assertion freshness rejects replay.

Links to artifacts and context:
- Threat model draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/rbacv2-threatdelta
- Pen-test report (redacted): drive/pen-test-2025/rbcaudit-report.pdf
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8412, https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8427
- Security guild review thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0SEC1234/p1610000000000

Next steps (this ticket owner):
- Finalize triage matrix with Security by 2025-01-17.
- Land initial HMAC-based audit immutability PR by 2025-01-31 (PR #8427).
- Land RBAC parser validation & decision cache eviction changes by 2025-02-07 (PR #8412).
- Schedule security sign-off and coordinate canary (target week of 2025-02-10).

Notes: prioritize minimal blast radius fixes that stop active exploit paths; follow-up work can expand to stronger cryptographic guarantees and UX improvements for admin flows.
